brief.interpretation: A single introductory sales email for a problem-aware small local business owner or marketer, centered on a practical weekly workflow rather than onboarding an existing user.
brief.reader:
Selected audience: Independent local business planning social posts.
Research context describes some members of this market, not this recipient's installed tools or experiences. Follow the campaign request when it scopes the job.
Observed situation (inferred; check applicability): not established
brief.reader_segment: Independent local business planning social posts
brief.promise: Buffer can support a simple weekly rhythm: schedule a few posts across connected social channels, then use basic post-performance data to inform the next batch.
brief.orientation: Buffer is a social media workspace where a small local business can schedule posts across connected channels and check basic results in the same dashboard.
brief.arc: In one compact email, move from a recognizable weekly task to the queue-and-review workflow, then make the Free plan's boundaries visible before inviting a plan comparison.
brief.sequence_rationale: Because the deliverable is exactly one concise email, it must introduce the product, demonstrate the workflow, disclose the relevant Free-plan limits, and provide a low-friction official next step without adding unrelated features or unsupported audience assumptions.

emails.job: Get the reader to compare Buffer's official plans after understanding one concrete weekly scheduling-and-review workflow and the Free plan's boundaries.
emails.single_idea: At the start of the week, queue a few posts across connected channels; after they publish, check each post's engagement, impressions, and other available performance data in Buffer before planning the next week.
emails.felt_need: If keeping several social channels supplied each week is part of the job, the reader needs a repeatable way to plan a small batch and learn from what was published.
emails.mechanism: Buffer combines scheduled posts per connected channel with Insights beside the content being measured. The Free plan can support this workflow with up to three connected channels and no more than 10 scheduled posts waiting per channel at one time; each published post frees a slot.
emails.belief_shift: Before: Buffer may sound like a broad social media tool with unclear relevance or limits. After: it is a concrete weekly queue-and-review workflow the reader can assess against transparent Free-plan boundaries.
must_not_say: Do not presume the reader currently uses native posting, another tool, a spreadsheet, or any particular workflow.
Do not promise follower, reach, engagement, revenue, or time-saving growth.
Do not describe the Free plan as unlimited: it allows up to three connected channels and 10 scheduled posts per channel at one time, with slots refilling after publication.
Do not imply every metric is available for every social network.
Do not add AI, comment management, collaboration, customer proof, paid-plan pricing, or a long channel list; they distract from the weekly workflow.
Do not frame this as onboarding for an existing Buffer user.
emails.objection: The reader may reasonably wonder whether the free entry is useful for a real weekly routine or conceals restrictive scheduling limits.
emails.tone: Plainspoken, practical, and lightly encouraging; concise rather than promotional.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether Buffer's Free plan can accommodate the business's number of channels and typical weekly queue, or whether a paid plan is worth considering.
emails.next_step_value: The official comparison shows Buffer's plan options and lets the reader assess the Free entry against its limit of up to three connected channels and 10 scheduled posts per channel at one time.
emails.next_step_limit: The pricing comparison does not establish which performance metrics will be available for the reader's specific social account types.
emails.subject_strategy: Signal the concrete weekly outcome—queue this week's posts, then review what worked—without hype, a growth promise, or a vague product introduction.

brief.voice_notes: Use Buffer's short, conversational cadence and second-person language. Prefer concrete verbs such as queue, publish, and check. State the Free-plan limits in the body, not in fine print.
